correctness.rationale: Exact disjoint monomial blocks give a two-sided unitary direct sum of the H-J normalized overlap matrix. Intersection of partition subspaces has dimension gcd(m,n); selected-row triangularity proves finite block rank. For n=m+1, polynomial triangularization of the exact symmetric Hahn difference matrix proves all eigenvalues j(j+1). Riemann sums prove continuous limiting levels. The standalone finite checker verifies cases but is not used as an infinite proof.

It does not itself derive the Hardy weighted-composition cross-adjoint identity, norm dichotomy or limiting distribution. Bare composition intertwining through I-M_z is not adjoint preserving.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary papers introduce weighted composition semigroup and isometries, but do not assert the mixed-adjoint overlap-block and gcd/Hahn hierarchy. Classical Hahn eigenvalues are explicitly acknowledged as prior. Published bare monomial composition reports concern a distinct, not unitarily equivalent operator. Priority risk remains for general canonical-correlation theory.
residual_risks: A prior canonical-correlation/principal-angle theorem for uniform interval partitions might imply the finite adjacent-base spectrum.
Some closely related published bare-composition records were accessible only as titles and abstracts, not full text.
Novelty is not independently certified; the classical Hahn eigenvalues are prior art.

value.rationale: The original arithmetic commuting isometries are naturally studied for cyclicity and invariant subspaces. The precise gcd norm dichotomy and all adjacent-base levels give a nontrivial operator-theoretic obstruction to double commutation, and the density describes the high-base limit of its entire finite block spectrum. They are not a mere relabeling of Hahn eigenvalues, because the exact cross-adjoint overlap reduction and arithmetic cases require separate proof.
